component.name: Doubao Murmur
豆包语音输入
component.summary: 使用豆包语音识别的语音输入工具

description.p: Doubao Murmur is a voice-to-text input tool that uses Doubao's ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) service to convert speech to text in real-time. Press the right Alt key to start dictating from anywhere; the transcription appears in a floating overlay and is pasted into whatever application had focus.
豆包语音输入是一款语音转文字工具，使用豆包的 ASR（自动语音识别）服务 实时将语音转换为文字。在任意应用中按下右 Alt 键即可开始说话，识别结果 显示在悬浮窗中，结束后自动粘贴回原来的输入框。

Asks you to log in again when the saved Doubao login has expired. The server drops such a connection without an error message, so recording used to end with an empty transcription and no prompt. A login the server rejects outright now gets the same prompt instead of a generic connection error.

Fixes auto-paste into terminals on Hyprland, which printed a literal "v" instead of the transcription. Terminal detection only asked KWin and xdotool, neither of which can see native Wayland windows there, so every terminal got Ctrl+V; it now asks hyprctl first. The overlay also follows the focused monitor on Hyprland instead of always opening on the first one.

Makes auto-paste reliable on plain X11 sessions. The paste keystroke now goes through xdotool so it honors a remapped Ctrl (such as ctrl:swapcaps, which used to send CapsLock+V), the window that had focus before recording is re-activated before pasting so the keystroke no longer lands on the overlay, and Electron apps such as VS Code now accept the synthetic Ctrl+V.

Keeps the last word or two of a transcription that used to go missing when you stopped recording. The service returns one result per audio message and holds the final word back until more audio arrives, so ending the stream abruptly meant that word was never transcribed; recording now ends with a short pad of silence, and the transcript is accepted once the results stop arriving rather than on the first one.

Fixes the global hotkey on Wayland sessions. The sandbox was never granted /dev/input, so the evdev listener could not start; on Wayland that is the only backend that works, because the preferred X11 listener cannot see keys sent to native Wayland windows.

Fixes auto-paste on Wayland desktops such as SteamOS. The clipboard copy silently failed without wl-clipboard on the host, which is now bundled, and the paste keystroke never reached native Wayland windows because xdotool only injects into XWayland; a uinput-based injector handles both Wayland and X11. Terminal windows are also detected correctly on Plasma Wayland now, so they receive Ctrl+Shift+V instead of a Ctrl+V that they swallowed as a control character.

A flaky network no longer forces you to log in again: cached credentials are cleared only when the server actively rejects them, not on handshake timeouts. Connecting also stays around half a second on networks with a blackholed IPv6 path.
Adds a native Windows build alongside macOS and Linux. No changes to the Linux app itself; the version is bumped so all three platforms ship under one release tag.

Auto-paste into the Warp terminal: its window class (dev.warp.Warp) was not recognized as a terminal, so the app sent Ctrl+V instead of Ctrl+Shift+V and Warp dropped the text (leaving a stray "v"). Warp is now in the terminal list and pastes correctly.

On-screen keyboard one-handed mode: widen from 22% to 35% of the screen so keys are large enough to tap (~6mm instead of ~4mm), and fix a keyboard reopened directly in a one-handed/split mode keeping a stale saved width and missing its compact styling. Width is now always derived from the current mode and monitor.

Recording overlay: wrap transcription text properly. Chinese has no spaces, so the default word-wrap found no break points and the text overflowed into a head-truncating ellipsis pinned at two lines. The overlay now wraps between characters and grows in height up to five lines before the oldest words scroll off.

Change the on-screen keyboard's global hotkey to Ctrl+Super+Shift (pure modifiers). The old Alt+Shift+F10+F11 chord leaked F-key escape sequences into focused terminals; modifier-only keys emit no characters, so nothing leaks.
On-screen keyboard: make key presses reliable on the touchscreen (fire on the native button click, drop the gesture/poll path that dropped touch-release events and could deadlock the keyboard)
Add an on-screen touch keyboard: full/split/one-handed layout modes, sticky modifiers, symbols layer, drag & resize, tray toggle, and the Alt+Shift+F10+F11 global hotkey
Add system tray icon (StatusNotifierItem) with status menu
